javascript.childprocess.exec.a0.summary: Executes a command through the host shell; treat user-controlled input as a command-injection boundary.

python.pickle.load.a0.summary: Deserializes a pickle stream and can execute code during object reconstruction.
python.pickle.load.a0.safe_pattern: Use a data-only format such as JSON when the payload is not fully trusted.

c.std.system.a0.summary: Passes a string to the system command processor; shell metacharacters make the boundary especially sensitive.
c.std.system.a0.safe_pattern: Avoid shell parsing; use a direct process API and fixed arguments.

javascript.shell-quote.quote.a0-ret.summary: Quotes a shell argument for a specific shell grammar. This is a sanitizer, not proof that the overall command is safe.
javascript.shell-quote.quote.a0-ret.safe_pattern: Prefer removing the shell boundary entirely; quote only as a constrained compatibility measure.

javascript.std.eval.a0.summary: Evaluates a string as JavaScript in the current execution context; untrusted text becomes executable code.
javascript.std.eval.a0.safe_pattern: Keep code and data separate. Use a parser or a constrained expression language when evaluation is unavoidable.

typescript.std.eval.a0.summary: Evaluates a string as JavaScript in the current execution context; untrusted text becomes executable code.
typescript.std.eval.a0.safe_pattern: Keep code and data separate. Use a parser or a constrained expression language when evaluation is unavoidable.

python.builtins.eval.a0.summary: Evaluates a Python expression with ambient globals and locals, making input-to-code transitions difficult to constrain.
python.builtins.eval.a0.safe_pattern: Parse structured data or expose a small allow-listed operation set instead of evaluating source text.

python.os.system.a0.summary: Hands a command string to the operating system shell, preserving shell expansion and metacharacter behavior.
python.os.system.a0.safe_pattern: Use subprocess with an argument list and shell disabled; validate each argument for its intended domain.

python.subprocess.run.a0.summary: Starts a process from caller-controlled arguments; the security boundary depends on argument construction and shell mode.
python.subprocess.run.a0.safe_pattern: Pass a sequence of fixed executable and arguments, keep shell=False, and constrain executable selection.

python.yaml.load.a0.summary: Loads YAML with a loader whose behavior depends on the selected constructor set; unsafe constructors can instantiate objects.
python.yaml.load.a0.safe_pattern: Use SafeLoader or a data-only YAML parser when documents are not fully trusted.

python.yaml.unsafeload.a0.summary: Explicitly enables YAML constructors that can create Python objects from input, making the deserializer a code-execution boundary.
python.yaml.unsafeload.a0.safe_pattern: Do not use this loader for attacker-controlled documents; prefer safe_load and a schema.

c.std.memcpy.a0.summary: Copies a caller-supplied byte count into a destination without inherent bounds checking.
c.std.memcpy.a0.safe_pattern: Carry destination capacity alongside the buffer and use a bounded operation with a checked length.

c.std.memcpy.a2.summary: Copies a caller-supplied byte count into a destination without inherent bounds checking.
c.std.memcpy.a2.safe_pattern: Carry destination capacity alongside the buffer and use a bounded operation with a checked length.

c.std.strcpy.a0.summary: Copies a NUL-terminated string without receiving the destination capacity, so a long source can overrun the buffer.
c.std.strcpy.a0.safe_pattern: Use a length-aware API and make truncation or rejection explicit.
c.std.strcpy.a0.safe_example: if (strlen(input) < sizeof buffer) memcpy(buffer, input, strlen(input) + 1);
c.std.strcpy.a0.limitations: A bounded copy still needs a policy for termination and truncation.

c.std.sprintf.a0.summary: Formats data into a fixed destination without a capacity argument; output length can exceed the buffer.
c.std.sprintf.a0.safe_pattern: Use a size-bounded formatter and handle truncation as an error.

c.sqlite3.exec.a1.summary: Executes SQL assembled as a string; concatenated input can become SQL syntax instead of data.
c.sqlite3.exec.a1.safe_pattern: Use prepared statements and bind values separately from the query text.

c.mysql.query.a1.summary: Sends a SQL string to MySQL; interpolated request data changes the grammar of the statement.
c.mysql.query.a1.safe_pattern: Use parameterized queries through the driver API.
c.mysql.query.a1.safe_example: Use a prepared statement with a bound parameter.

javascript.pg.client.query.a0.summary: Sends a SQL command through node-postgres; string interpolation can turn input into SQL syntax.
javascript.pg.client.query.a0.safe_pattern: Pass values through the query parameter array instead of concatenating them.

javascript.std.queryrawunsafe.a0.summary: Executes a raw query without the parameterization guarantees of a higher-level query builder.
javascript.std.queryrawunsafe.a0.safe_pattern: Use the library's parameterized query form and reserve raw SQL for fixed, reviewed text.

javascript.std.executerawunsafe.a0.summary: Executes raw database text by design; caller input can cross directly into query syntax.

javascript.execa.command.a0.summary: Parses a command string before launching a child process; shell-like input becomes part of process selection and arguments.
javascript.execa.command.a0.safe_pattern: Use an argument-array command form and constrain the executable.

javascript.shelljs.exec.a0.summary: Runs a shell command string from JavaScript and preserves shell expansion behavior.
javascript.shelljs.exec.a0.safe_pattern: Use a direct process API with explicit arguments and no shell parsing.

javascript.jsyaml.load.a0.summary: Parses YAML with constructor behavior controlled by loader options; unsafe constructors can create objects from input.
javascript.jsyaml.load.a0.safe_pattern: Choose a safe schema and loader for untrusted documents.

python.pickle.loads.a0.summary: Deserializes bytes using Python pickle and can execute code during reconstruction.

python.marshal.load.a0.summary: Reads Python marshal data intended for internal use, not as a safe interchange format.
python.marshal.load.a0.safe_pattern: Treat marshal bytes as trusted implementation data and use JSON or another validated format at boundaries.

python.ast.literaleval.a0-ret.summary: Evaluates a limited Python literal grammar, but deeply nested or large input can still exhaust interpreter resources.
python.ast.literaleval.a0-ret.safe_pattern: Bound input size and nesting before evaluation, or parse against an explicit schema.
python.ast.literaleval.a0-ret.limitations: Literal-only syntax does not make resource exhaustion impossible.
